description: LyraCore, sıradan bulut bağımlısı IoT mimarilerinin çok ötesinde, tamamen uç birimde (edge-first) ve sıfır altyapı/bağlantı gerektiren ortamlarda bile kusursuz çalışan yerel akıllı sistemler inşa etme vizyonuyla doğmuş yüksek teknolojili bir girişim/takım ekosistemidir.
summary:
BLACK HOLE LAB is an interactive black-hole laboratory that runs exact Kerr and Schwarzschild physics entirely in
    the browser — no backend, no approximations. A pure TypeScript engine (TanStack Start, Three.js) computes 16
    observables in real time: horizons, ergosphere, photon spheres, the Bardeen shadow, null-geodesic lensing, time
    dilation, tidal acceleration and black-hole thermodynamics. The engine is validated against real observations:
    theoretical shadow diameters agree with Event Horizon Telescope measurements at 0.98σ (M87) and 0.47σ (Sgr A),
    while S2 precession matches VLT/GRAVITY data. Users explore presets, export scientific figures and share live
    views — every readout derives from first principles, with nothing hardcoded.
details:
Black Hole Lab is an interactive black-hole laboratory that computes exact Kerr and Schwarzschild relativistic

physics entirely in the browser — no backend, no approximations, nothing hardcoded. Users control mass,

dimensionless spin, observer distance and inclination with sliders, and a pure TypeScript engine recalculates 16

observables in real time: event horizons, ergosphere, photon spheres, the Bardeen shadow, null-geodesic light

bending, time dilation, tidal acceleration and black-hole thermodynamics, including Hawking temperature. Every

readout on screen is derived from first principles at the current slider state, and the same engine module backs

the UI, the automated test suite and a reproducible validation script.

The engine is validated against real observations. Theoretical shadow diameters agree with Event Horizon

Telescope measurements at 0.98σ for M87* and 0.47σ for Sgr A* — both within 1σ. The lab also fetches live NASA

data: M87, Sgr A and Cygnus X-1 imagery from the NASA Image and Video Library API, and the Cygnus X-1 catalog

row from NASA HEASARC Xamin (TAP service), so no science value on screen is hand-entered or cached.

The benefit is accessibility: it turns graduate-level relativity into something a student, teacher or curious

visitor can experiment with directly — see how spin changes shadow size, compare scale anchors (M87*'s shadow

spans 11× Neptune's orbit), and export results as PNG figures, JSON data or WEBM animations, with shareable views

encoded in the URL. The intended impact is to make exact relativistic physics — normally locked behind

specialized software — open, visual and verifiable for anyone with a browser.

The project is built with TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start (Router/Query), Vite, Three.js

(@react-three/fiber), Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, recharts and vitest (34 passing tests), deployed on Cloudflare

Workers. The physics is client-side for latency-free 60 fps interaction; the only server component is a minimal

bridge for NASA HEASARC CORS.

Our team's guiding factors were scientific honesty (no fudge factors), reproducibility (anyone can rerun the EHT

validation with one command) and clarity: every visualization exists to make an exact calculation visible.
projectRefs: Event Horizon Telescope — First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results (ApJL 875, L1)
Event Horizon Telescope — Sgr A* Results (ApJL 930, L12)
GRAVITY Collaboration — Detection of the Schwarzschild Precession in the Orbit of the Star S2 (A&A       636, L5)
